name: KAT6B-related multiple congenital anomalies syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnostic criteria for KAT6B-related multiple congenital anomalies syndrome

criteria.description: Hypoplasia or aplasia of the patella
Congenital genitourinary malformations such as cryptorchidism or hydronephrosis
Characteristic facial dysmorphisms including blepharophimosis, ptosis, and broad nasal bridge
Global developmental delay or intellectual disability
Additional skeletal anomalies such as scoliosis or joint contractures

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: patellar hypoplasia/aplasia, genitourinary anomalies, and distinctive facial features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular confirmation by identification of pathogenic KAT6B variants supports diagnosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic facial dysmorphisms (blepharophimosis, ptosis, broad nasal bridge)
searchTerms: droopy eyelids and wide nose bridge
narrow eye openings and broad nose
distinctive facial features with eyelid droop
birth defects of urinary and genital organs
global delay in growth and skills

occasional.symptomName: Congenital heart defects (e.g., atrial septal defect)
searchTerms: heart defects like atrial septal hole
abnormal heart structure present at birth

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; thyroid function tests may reveal hypothyroidism
imaging: Radiographs showing patellar hypoplasia or aplasia
genetic: Pathogenic variants in the KAT6B gene detected by molecular genetic testing
other: Developmental assessment confirming global developmental delay

distinguishingFeatures: Overlapping features but distinguished by specific KAT6B mutation spectrum and clinical presentation
Considered part of the KAT6B-related spectrum but may differ in severity and specific skeletal anomalies
Facial dysmorphism and developmental delay but lacks patellar anomalies

redFlags: Absence or severe hypoplasia of patella in a neonate
Congenital genitourinary malformations with developmental delay
Characteristic facial dysmorphisms combined with multiple congenital anomalies
references: Clayton-Smith J, et al. Genitopatellar syndrome and Say-Barber-Biesecker-Young-Simpson syndrome: clinical and molecular overlap. Am J Med Genet A. 2011.
Simpson MA, et al. Mutations in KAT6B, encoding a histone acetyltransferase, cause genitopatellar syndrome. Nat Genet. 2012.
Orphanet: KAT6B-related multiple congenital anomalies syndrome. Orphanet Report Series. 2023.
